text.String: Source-first smoke. Native-owner metadata. Kain-authored mesh data. Qt is the current presentation fallback.
Kain owns the runtime contract here. The smoke is source-first, the buttons change the shell mood, and the scene stays Kain-authored instead of living off a bundle example.
bgfx feels immediate: cross-platform, direct, and stable enough to anchor the smoke.
Kain owns the runtime contract. Qt is the presentation fallback.
baseline lane for the first real runtime-backed viewport.
The new 3D runtime should feel like authored product software, not a thin renderer demo.
bgfx feels immediate: cross-platform, direct, and stable enough to anchor the smoke.
filament feels premium: materials, lighting, and presentation should read expensive.
diligent feels surgical: explicit passes, graph control, and compute depth.
the-forge feels raw: low-level substrate, bridge-first, and deliberately close to the metal.
The authored mesh data used for the central plinth and stable massing.
A repeating vertical system that gives the scene depth and rhythm.
A luminous ring around the center mass that keeps the scene feeling premium.
A lifted frame that keeps the scene readable as a scene instead of a cube room.
The launcher now includes smoke.kn directly, so the authored surface is the thing being booted rather than a generated runtime bundle example.
geometry_fixture is the runtime scene profile, and the Windows native viewport branch now knows about it as a first-class scene name.
